Communities should be able to coordinate through encrypted group communication and participant- or community-controlled hosting, reducing dependence on a single platform for their data and continuity. Personal privacy intermediaries

A participant-configured agent can mediate interactions with networks, applications, forms, and connected devices. It can help apply permissions to differently sensitive flows, filter incoming material according to stated preferences, and restrict device interactions to networks the participant trusts. Its actions and filters should remain visible, inspectable, and revocable.

A browser or embedded data lens can complement that intermediary by showing collection and tracking while an interaction is happening. The lens should distinguish observed activity from inferred activity, so participants can act on useful evidence without mistaking the tool for a complete inventory of hidden processing.

Privacy transport and civic sandbox trials

A decentralized privacy-routing mesh is one implementation option for reducing exposure of interaction, contribution, and identity-resolution traffic. Multiparty relays and onion routing are candidate approaches. Trials should keep routing optional and evaluate protection, operator dependencies, accessibility, and performance before wider adoption. DP7 addresses compatibility with participant-chosen privacy infrastructure, and DP17 addresses possible relay funding.

Local, multi-sector civic sandboxes, including the proposed UMi Insecurity Initiatives and Sandbox environments, can test whether privacy mechanisms are understandable, equitable, and effective in practice. A pilot’s institutional setting is evidence to examine, not proof of the mechanism’s success.
